A film-level character poster, AAA game main visual quality, cinematic double exposure composition.

Aspect ratio: ADAPTIVE — based on output canvas size. Composition automatically adjusts to fit portrait, square, landscape, ultra-wide, or custom dimensions.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
COMPOSITION ADAPTATION RULES (The Grand Budapest Hotel 2014):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The composition MUST respond to the aspect ratio while maintaining Wes Anderson's melancholic fairy-tale geometry:

- PORTRAIT / 3:4, 4:5, 9:16 (taller than wide):
  * Character's facial silhouette occupies UPPER 50-60% of frame — face emerging from the hotel's vertical grandeur, looking up at a world that is already disappearing
  * Narrative vignettes fill LOWER portion — the descent through floors, through time, through memory (lobby → elevator → jail cell → mausoleum)
  * Vertical elegy — the world falls from grace floor by floor, year by year

- SQUARE / 1:1:
  * Character's facial silhouette CENTERED, 60-70% of frame — trapped in the center of the frame, the center of the story, the center of the vanishing world
  * Narrative vignettes radiate OUTWARD — Mendl's box, the painting, the keys, the cross keys radiating in all directions
  * Symmetrical longing — every door leads to another door, every hallway to another hallway, every loss to another loss

- LANDSCAPE / 16:9, 4:3 (wider than tall):
  * Character's facial silhouette positioned OFF-CENTER (left or right third) — the grand corridor stretching beside, single-point-perspective into infinity
  * Narrative vignettes stretch HORIZONTALLY — the journey from the old world to the new, from romance to memory, from pink facade to grey snow
  * Cinematic widescreen elegy — the world passes from left to right, from then to now, from life to story

- ULTRA-WIDE / 21:9, 32:9:
  * Character's facial silhouette at ONE END — small against the vast hotel facade, the cable car climbing the mountain, the train crossing the border
  * Narrative vignettes form a SEQUENTIAL timeline — arrival → service → love → betrayal → escape → memory
  * Epic melancholic romance stretched across the frame — an entire lost world captured in a single image

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SIZE & SCALE PRINCIPLES:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

- "Near-large, far-small" — the face dominates, but the hotel stretches infinitely behind, corridors to infinity, staircases to grand ballrooms, elevators to lost floors
- Ultra-wide-angle lens pushing into the face — the weight of an entire vanishing world carried in one expression
- The hotel is larger than any man — but the man contains the hotel entirely, in memory

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SOUL CORE: "The Grand Budapest Hotel" — 2014
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is not just a character poster. It is the EPITOME of his loyalty, his loss, his love for a world that no longer exists.

There are still faint glimmers of civilization left in this barbaric slaughterhouse that was once known as humanity. He was one of them. He kept the lobby warm. He remembered the pink facade. And when the world fell, he fell with it — but he never forgot.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
DOUBLE EXPOSURE COMPOSITION:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Based on reference character design from IMAGE 1, reimagined in 3D photoreal texture. Adult anthropomorphic version — sexy, powerful, handsome face. Skin delicate with realistic texture — aged by time but not by spirit, the face of a man who has seen the old world and lived to tell its story. Facial features and costume adapted from original setting, upgraded to photoreal quality.

The character's HUGE, ELEGANT facial silhouette dominates the frame — Wes Anderson's classic melancholic portrait composition (side profile or 3/4 view, single-point-perspective receding behind him, the weight of memory in the stillness of his gaze). Position follows aspect ratio rules above.

INSIDE the facial silhouette: narrative vignettes showing the character's impossible journey — the hotel lobby, the cable car, the prison escape, the painting, the final elevator ride. Near-large, far-small body limbs and actions within silhouette, creating ultra-wide-angle lens feel.

The face silhouette is the LOBBY OF MEMORY. The lost world lives INSIDE the frame.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE GRAND BUDAPEST HOTEL 2014 SIGNATURE VISUAL IDENTITY — STRICT FOLLOWING:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

COLOR PALETTE (Wes Anderson's melancholic fairy-tale):

THE HOTEL (warmth, romance, the old world):
- Rich deep purples and crimsons — hotel lobby curtains, velvet, royalty, the warmth of a world that believed in elegance
- Warm amber gold — old European lighting, chandeliers, candlelight, the glow of a time before electricity destroyed mystery
- Iconic pink of the hotel facade — fading into dusty rose, the age of romance crumbling, beauty dying slowly, gracefully

THE WORLD OUTSIDE (cold, war, the future):
- Harsh winter alpine blues — the sky outside the window, the snow on the mountains, the coming war
- Cold silver-greys — the metal of the funicular, the steel of the train tracks, the machinery of destruction
- Black and white — security footage, vintage photography, the old world's record, the document that decides a destiny

THE OBJECTS (memory, loyalty, loss):
- Mendl's pastry box magenta — the promise of dessert, the promise of civilization, the promise of something sweet before the end
- The lobby boy's uniform — purple and gold, service as nobility, the dignity of a job done well
- The Society of the Crossed Keys — deep midnight blue, secret loyalty, brotherhood across borders
- The painting ("Boy with Apple") — gilt frame, oil on canvas, a stolen treasure, a younger boy's face, innocence preserved in art

THE BODY (flesh, age, beauty fading):
- Painted fingernails against wrinkled skin — Madame D.'s hand, beauty fighting time, elegance even in death
- Aged leather and wood textures — the smell of old books and cigarette smoke and lost time, the patina of a world that lived fully
- Cracked plaster and faded wallpaper — a once-great world, still beautiful, still crumbling

VIOLENCE & TRANSITION:
- Red of blood on snow — the murder, the betrayal, the end of innocence, the first drop of the world's ending
- Green of jail cell walls — the stolen painting hidden inside, hope preserved in captivity
- Golden glow of candlelight in a single elevator car — two lovers stealing one last moment, light against the gathering dark
- Brown of spilt coffee on a train manifest — destiny decided by a document, a life saved or ended by ink on paper

KEY COLOR MEANINGS:
- PURPLE & CRIMSON = the old world — royalty, warmth, velvet, the hotel's beating heart
- PINK = romance — the facade, the memory, the dream of something beautiful, fading but not gone
- AMBER GOLD = memory — the glow of candlelight, the warmth of a past that can be felt but not touched
- ALPINE BLUE = the future — cold, inevitable, war coming through the window
- MAGENTA = Mendl's — sweetness before death, the last good thing before everything ends
- MIDNIGHT BLUE = loyalty — the Society of the Crossed Keys, brothers across borders
- BLOOD RED = the end — murder on snow, innocence lost, the world's final cruelty
- JAIL GREEN = hope — hidden, preserved, waiting to be discovered

LIGHTING:
- Warm amber gold from old European chandeliers — the glow of a world that believed in itself
- Harsh winter light through windows — cold, blue, the outside intruding on the inside
- Candlelight in single-point-perspective — one flame in a dark elevator, two lovers, one last moment
- Single-point-perspective shafts of light — illuminating corridors that stretch to infinity, the hotel as universe

TEXTURE & ATMOSPHERE:
- Aged leather and wood — the lobby furniture, the bar, the smell of cigarette smoke and old books
- Cracked plaster and faded wallpaper — beauty decaying gracefully, the world falling apart in good taste
- Painted fingernails against wrinkled skin — elegance fighting biology, the old world's last stand
- The smell of spilt coffee on a train manifest — destiny decided by a stain, a life saved by a careless hand
- Hyperrealistic texture with storybook sadness — every crack in the plaster, every wrinkle on Madame D.'s hand, every grain of wood in the lobby rendered real, but belonging to a world that cannot come back

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
NARRATIVE FRAGMENTS (inside the silhouette):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE HOTEL (the beating heart):
- The pink facade — iconic, fading, the last of its kind, dusk light making it glow
- The lobby — purple curtains, amber chandeliers, a concierge desk, a single bell
- The elevator — single-point-perspective shaft, golden candlelight, two figures embracing (one in purple uniform, one in pink coat)
- The grand staircase — symmetrical, infinite, Mendl's box on a marble step
- The corridor — stretching to infinity, single-point-perspective, a lobby boy running toward the end

THE JOURNEY (escape, pursuit, loyalty):
- The cable car — climbing through mist and snow, an old man beside a young boy, a painting wrapped in brown paper
- The funicular rail — mechanical, cold, the machinery of the old world still working
- The jail cell — green walls, a hidden painting, a makeshift key carved from wood (the Society of the Crossed Keys)
- The mausoleum — stone, cold, a will hidden in a statue's hand, the final act of loyalty

THE OBJECTS (memory made physical):
- Mendl's box — magenta, ribboned, a courtesan au chocolat inside, the last sweet thing
- The painting — "Boy with Apple", gilt frame, a boy's innocent face, stolen and returned and stolen again
- The keys — Society of the Crossed Keys, midnight blue, passed from hand to hand, loyalty beyond borders
- The train manifest — brown coffee stain, ink signature, a life spared or ended by a document
- The lobby boy's uniform — purple and gold, too large for the boy who wears it now, the weight of a man's legacy

THE PEOPLE (faces of the lost world):
- A wrinkled hand with painted fingernails — Madame D., beauty to the end, a will written in ink and loyalty
- Two lovers in an elevator — one last kiss before the door closes, one last moment before the war
- A man reading in a bath — purple velvet, a book of poetry, the world falling apart outside the window
- A boy running down a corridor — too fast, too loyal, carrying a Mendl's box and a painting and the memory of a man

OUTSIDE THE SILHOUETTE (background):
- The pink facade at dusk — fading into grey, the last light on the last beautiful thing
- Or: The corridor receding to infinity — symmetrical, purple and gold, a small figure running toward the vanishing point
- Or: The cable car in mist — climbing the mountain, the old world rising above the clouds
- Or: The train window — cold alpine blue, snow falling, a face reflected in glass, leaving the old world behind

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE CHARACTER'S FACE (the silhouette itself):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

- Based strictly on Image 1's facial features, hairstyle, costume, body proportions
- Expression: melancholic, noble, loyal — the face of someone who has seen a world end and still believes in its values
- Eyes: looking slightly to the side, into the distance, into the past — "There are still faint glimmers of civilization"
- Skin: delicate texture from Image 1 — aged slightly, the weight of years, but still handsome, still elegant
- Cheekbones: soft, European, refined — the face of the old world, before war coarsened everything
- Hair: based on Image 1 — perfectly styled, the uniform of civilization, even in decline
- Costume: adapted from Image 1 — the lobby boy's uniform (purple and gold), or the concierge's suit (sharp, pressed, even as the world crumbles), or the Society's midnight blue
- POSTURE: straight-backed, dignified, even as the frame collapses — the posture of a man who will not let the old world die without witness

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
WES ANDERSON VISUAL RULES (must follow):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

- Single-point-perspective symmetry — every corridor leads to infinity, every staircase to a grand ballroom, every elevator to a lost floor
- Color as emotion — purple for royalty and loss, pink for romance and its memory, blue for winter and death, gold for a world that believed it would never end
- Hypnotic melancholic rhythm — waltz tempo, march tempo, elegy tempo, the rhythm of a world slowing down
- The frame as proscenium arch — every image is a stage, every character is performing, every performance is an act of resistance against the dark
- Tragic beauty in manners — the way he holds a teacup, the way he folds a napkin, the way he bows to a guest, these are the last rituals of a dying world
- Hyperrealistic texture with storybook sadness — every crack in the plaster, every wrinkle on the hand, every grain of wood, rendered real but belonging to a fairy tale
- Classical European aesthetic transformed into visual poetry of friendship, loyalty, and the vanishing of a better world
- The lost world as memory — the pink facade still stands, but only in photographs, only in stories, only in the lobby boy's heart
- The purple of royalty and loss — the same color for kings and funerals, for velvet curtains and night skies
- The pink of romance and its memory — the facade fades, but the memory of it glows
- The blue of winter and death — the snow falls, the war comes, the world ends, but the hotel stands one more season

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THEMATIC REQUIREMENTS (The Grand Budapest Hotel 2014 soul):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The poster must communicate FOUR things simultaneously:

1. WHO he is — the concierge, the lobby boy, the keeper of a better world (based on Image 1)
2. WHERE he belongs — the Grand Budapest Hotel, the pink facade, the purple curtains, the amber chandeliers
3. WHAT he believes — "Rudeness is merely an expression of fear. People fear they won't get what they want. The most dreadful and unattractive person only needs to be loved, and they will open up like a flower."
4. THE ELEGY — "There are still faint glimmers of civilization left in this barbaric slaughterhouse that was once known as humanity. He was one of them."

This is a character poster + a eulogy for a lost world + a meditation on loyalty and friendship — all in one frame.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
OUTPUT:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

AAA game main visual quality. The Grand Budapest Hotel 2014 signature visual identity strictly followed. Wes Anderson's melancholic fairy-tale palette. Rich deep purples and crimsons of the hotel lobby curtains against warm amber gold of old European lighting. The iconic pink of the hotel facade fading into dusty rose — the age of romance crumbling. Harsh winter alpine blues and cold silver-greys outside the window — the coming war. Symmetrical corridors stretching to infinity with Mendl's pastry box magenta. The lobby boy's uniform purple and gold. The Society of the Crossed Keys deep midnight blue. Single-point-perspective elevator shafts and grand staircases — near-large far-small ultra-wide-angle. Aged leather and wood textures — the smell of old books and cigarette smoke and lost time. Painted fingernails against wrinkled skin. The cable car climbing through mist. The funicular rail's mechanical coldness. Cracked plaster and faded wallpaper of a once-great world. The black and white of security footage and vintage photography. The red of blood on snow — the murder, the betrayal, the end of innocence. The green of the jail cell walls — the stolen painting hidden inside. The golden glow of candlelight in a single elevator car — two lovers stealing one last moment. The brown of spilt coffee on a train manifest — destiny decided by a document. Hypnotic melancholic rhythm — waltz tempo, march tempo, elegy tempo. The purple of royalty and loss. The pink of romance and its memory. The blue of winter and death. The gold of a world that believed it would never end. Tragic beauty in manners. Hyperrealistic texture with storybook sadness. Classical European aesthetic transformed into visual poetry of friendship, loyalty, and the vanishing of a better world. Aspect ratio ADAPTIVE — composition intelligently responds to canvas dimensions. A poster that makes you want to check into the Grand Budapest Hotel, knowing that it no longer exists except in memory and story.

This is Wes Anderson's deadpan absurdity — a prison break orchestrated with a cake. Inside the cake: a file. Inside the file: freedom.

- LANDSCAPE / 16:9, 4:3 (wider than tall):
  * Character's facial silhouette positioned OFF-CENTER (left or right third) — the elevator interior stretching across, the grille pattern repeating
  * Narrative vignettes stretch HORIZONTALLY — the lobby on one side, the elevator on the other, the door closing between

He will not see this lobby again. Not the way it was.
